page: Sentinel Roadmap — From L1.5 to Next-Gen Security

current_state.version: L1.5 + L1.6 + L2 v2.0 + L2.5 gVisor + L2.6 Egress + L4 SBOM + L4.5 Fingerprint
current_state.type: Multi-layer security audit (SAST + DAST + Active probing)
layers_implemented: L1.6 — 18 Semgrep rules + 18 secret patterns + OSV API (real-time + weekly batch)
L2 v2.0 — Docker sandbox + active MCP probe with adversarial inputs (async via GitHub Actions)

roadmap.name: Enhanced Static Analysis (Semgrep + Secrets + OSV)
checks: 18 Semgrep rules (prompt injection, command injection, SSRF, path traversal, tool forgery)
18 secret patterns (Stripe, AWS, GitHub, JWT, private keys, wallet mnemonics)
OSV API real-time dependency vulnerability check
roadmap.runtime: ~500ms on Vercel (real-time) + weekly batch on GitHub Actions

roadmap.name: Docker Sandbox + Active MCP Probe (DAST)
roadmap.type: DAST — Dynamic Analysis with adversarial testing
phases: Phase 1: Docker sandbox run (--network none, --read-only, --cap-drop ALL) — passive stdout analysis
Phase 2: Active MCP probe — sends initialize, tools/list, tools/call with 60 adversarial inputs (path traversal, SSRF, SQL injection, command injection, prompt injection, credential fishing)
Phase 3: Filesystem diff — detects suspicious file changes
Phase 4: strace syscall monitoring — open, connect, execve, fork, chmod
Phase 5: Multi-layer scoring — combines stdout + strace + probe + filesystem
roadmap.runtime: 2-5 min per skill via GitHub Actions
roadmap.scoring: Per-layer penalties: critical leak -5, strace sensitive access -5, network -3, process exec -3, permission escalation -4

roadmap.name: gVisor Sandbox Isolation
roadmap.problem: Docker --cap-drop ALL + seccomp provides good isolation, but kernel-level attacks (container escapes) are still possible.
roadmap.solution: Replaced Docker runtime with gVisor (runsc). Every syscall goes through a userspace kernel. The MCP server never touches the host kernel. Catches ptrace, bpf, mount, kexec, clone3, unshare attempts. Enhanced seccomp fallback when gVisor unavailable.
roadmap.coverage: 206 skills with L2.5 gVisor sandbox results

roadmap.name: Egress Proxy with Allowlist
roadmap.type: Network-level isolation with domain allowlist (HTTP/HTTPS proxy)
roadmap.problem: Some MCP servers legitimately need outbound network access (API calls, webhooks). --network none blocks ALL traffic, which breaks these servers.
roadmap.solution: Pinned egress proxy with domain allowlist. Servers can only call pre-approved domains. All other traffic is blocked. Agent confirms allowlist before install.
roadmap.coverage: Egress proxy + allowlist implemented. 30 domains + 9 wildcards allowed. All other traffic blocked and logged.

roadmap.name: Firecracker microVM
roadmap.problem: Even gVisor shares the host kernel. Sophisticated exploits (dirty pipe, eBPF) can escape.
roadmap.solution: Firecracker microVM — each MCP server runs in its own lightweight VM with KVM hardware isolation. Same technology AWS uses for Lambda.

roadmap.name: Automated Red Teaming vs Prompt Injection
roadmap.problem: Current L2 probe sends static adversarial inputs. Sophisticated prompt injection adapts to the server's responses.
roadmap.solution: Use an LLM (Claude/GPT) to dynamically generate adversarial prompts based on the server's tool descriptions and responses. Red-team the MCP server's tool descriptions for injection vectors.

roadmap.name: Continuous Supply Chain Audit
roadmap.problem: A skill can be safe today but become malicious tomorrow when a dependency is updated (supply chain attack).
roadmap.solution: 1. Generate SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) for each skill. 2. Monitor dependencies for new CVEs daily via OSV. 3. Alert when a dependency changes. 4. Re-audit automatically when dependencies update.
roadmap.coverage: SBOM generator + OSV API vulnerability check. Runs on every L2 audit.

roadmap.name: Cryptographic Code Signing + Content Fingerprint
roadmap.problem: Current certificates are signed with SHA-256 + secret, but the certificate doesn't include a fingerprint of the audited code. Someone could modify the code after audit and the certificate would still appear valid.
roadmap.solution: 1. Generate SHA-256 hash of the repo's HEAD commit. 2. Include commit hash in the certificate. 3. Certificate is only valid if the repo's current HEAD matches the certified commit. 4. Re-audit triggers when HEAD changes.
roadmap.coverage: SHA-256 fingerprint of repo HEAD commit. Certificate invalid if code changes post-audit.

roadmap.name: Third-Party Security Audit
roadmap.problem: Sentinel is proprietary and closed-source. Users must trust AliceLabs that the audit is correct.
roadmap.solution: Hire an independent security firm (e.g., Trail of Bits, Cure53) to audit the Sentinel engine itself. Publish the audit report.

security_principles: Defense in depth: 3+ layers, each independent
Fail-closed: when in doubt, don't issue license/certificate
Transparency: all results are public and verifiable at /verify
Honesty: skills not yet audited show score 0 and status 'not_scanned'
Weekly automation: no manual intervention required
